prompt: Redesign the information architecture of a mature B2B application's settings. Existing controls are split across account, workspace, project, member, integration, security, billing, automation, and data-retention pages; labels were added by different teams; some destinations are duplicated; permissions vary by role; deep links are common in support; and customers report that they cannot predict where a control lives. Produce an implementation-ready IA proposal without redesigning control behavior or visual styling.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Account, workspace, project, member, integration, security, billing, automation, and retention concepts are organized from an explicit scope/relationship model rather than team ownership or current page history.
Each control has a predictable primary location; alternate paths or cross-links are intentional and do not create multiple ambiguous canonical destinations.
Labels are grounded in supplied customer/support search terms and concept meaning, with renamed concepts or redirects handled explicitly rather than invented from internal jargon.

Role/permission differences and common deep links preserve orientation: unavailable controls are handled intentionally and a deep-linked user can determine the control's scope and surrounding location.
The IA includes migration, growth, and governance risks without inventing arbitrary maximum item counts or redesigning individual control behavior/visual styling.
